claims.text: Simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosive exposure dynamically refine the HEA near-surface microstructure.
The mechanically induced surface layer is nanocrystalline or partially amorphous.
The refined surface layer promotes rapid and stable passive-oxide-film formation.
Formation of the refined near-surface layer reduces wear.
Passivation associated with the refined layer reduces corrosion.
The HEA initially has a conventional coarse or mixed bulk microstructure.
Moderate combined mechanical and corrosive stresses permit dynamic surface refinement.
Moderate combined stresses permit oxide redeposition.
The mechanically induced nanocrystalline or amorphous layer acts as a scaffold for a coherent protective oxide film.
Wear deformation supplies sufficient strain to refine the surface grain structure.
The resulting high density of grain boundaries supplies nucleation sites for oxide growth.
Enhanced passivation competes successfully with localized film breakdown.
Combined tribocorrosion produces a lower wear rate than the isolated-environment baselines.
Combined tribocorrosion produces a lower corrosion current density than the isolated-environment baselines.
Combined tribocorrosion improves passive-film stability relative to the isolated-environment baselines.
A sample exposed only to mechanical wear lacks dynamic wear-induced surface refinement.
A sample exposed only to corrosion lacks dynamic wear-induced surface refinement.
Very high mechanical loads disrupt formation or protective operation of the refined and passivated layer.
Elevated temperatures disrupt formation or protective operation of the refined and passivated layer.
Excessively aggressive corrosive chemistries disrupt formation or protective operation of the refined and passivated layer.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism state that mechanical wear drives surface refinement, but the baseline states that a wear-only sample lacks dynamic wear-induced refinement. The cited CoCrFeMnNi study also reports an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer formed during wear in an inert environment.
